Peter,
We are coming up on my favorite event of the year: the Golden Tennis Shoe Awards.
You see, I never planned to take part in politics. But when the state threatened to shut down my kids’ preschool program, I drove to Olympia to fight for it. And while I was there, a male legislator told me that I couldn’t make a difference because I was “just a mom in tennis shoes.” I got angry, but I also got into action. There was no way I was going to let that stop me from fighting for my community and going on to serve as the first woman – and first mom – representing Washington state in the U.S. Senate.
That’s why each year at the Golden Tennis Shoe Awards, I recognize a few people from Washington state who stood up despite the odds and overcame big obstacles to make a difference in their communities.
**[**Do you know a hero in your community who deserves to be recognized for their work at the Golden Tennis Shoe Awards this year? Nominate them now.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137850172/642152330/-1685103362?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&amounts=5,25,50,100,250&code=jtk717-fr-nd&refcode=jtk717-fr-nd&recurring=0&sustainers=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MjMyODdlZS0xN2EwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GMBuQA45_JhEMU_oux5_G19mWh_nAPzFcu-Ydfq_fH4=&emci=b9d402a3-df9f-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&emdi=723287ee-17a0-f111-9b33-0022482a9f1d&ceid=13116610)**
**If you know someone from Washington state who has gone above and beyond to create a positive change in their community, I want to hear their story, so I can recognize their dedication to fighting for what they believe in.**

Stats like this from California are the canary in the coal mine, Team. Kern County went from 332 uncounted, late ballots in 2024 to 3,303 in 2025. 📅 **August 24th Update** 🗳️ **Noteworthy Events** Last Tuesday, I attended an “issues” policy briefing focused on likely general‐election voters.On Wednesday morning, I met with GOP Congressional candidate Jay Feely, who is running to replace Congressman David Schweikert in District 1. Later that day, I joined a Colorado River water update hosted by the Central Arizona Project (CAP). CAP and the Arizona Department of Water Resources continue working with water users across the Lower Basin states—Arizona, California, and Nevada—as well as the federal government, on a two‐year agreement designed to provide stability for CAP users and the entire Colorado River system.
On Saturday morning, I joined Jay Feely along with other elected officials for the grand opening of his campaign headquarters in Scottsdale.💧 **Arizona Water Update** Late last week, the federal government finalized a two‐year emergency plan to protect the Colorado River system. The plan imposes deep water cuts on Lower Basin states while sparing Upper Basin states (Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, New Mexico) from mandatory reductions.The Colorado River supplies water to 40 million people across seven states, and federal officials say the action was necessary after years of drought, shrinking reservoirs, and stalled negotiations.📉 What This Means for ArizonaArizona will face major water reductions in 2027 and 2028, with the possibility of even deeper cuts after 2028 if conditions worsen. These reductions affect:
* 🏙️ cities and towns
* 🚜 agriculture and food production
* 🪶 tribal communities
* 📈 long‐term water planning and conservation efforts

The federal plan places a disproportionate burden on Arizona, as Upper Basin states will not share in mandatory reductions. These future cuts pose a serious threat to our state’s long‐term water security.⚠️ Why the Federal Government Stepped InDisagreements between the Upper and Lower Basin states prevented a seven‐state consensus. With key river‐management agreements expiring at the end of 2026—and reservoir levels at historic lows—the federal government intervened to prevent:
* ⚡ hydropower shutdowns
* 🏗️ infrastructure breakdowns
* 📉 further declines in Lake Mead and Lake Powell

The new plan serves as a bridge until a long‐term post‐2026 operating framework can be negotiated.🔭 What Comes NextNow that the 2027–2028 cuts are set, the seven states must negotiate a new long‐term management plan for the river. Discussions continue regarding the imbalance in reductions and whether Arizona will pursue legal action in response to the federal decision.🗳️ **What’s on Your November Ballot?** There are 71 days until the November election. Early ballots will be mailed on October 7th. body:
| | | Hi Peter, Today was another landmark day in what’s turning out to be an epic battle over mail-in voting. If you’re following along, this is the Trump Executive Order / USPS saga where the federal government wants to insert postal workers between you and your ballot. Today, **the Supreme Court lifted one of two court orders** that Colorado and many other states had won in federal court back in June. These orders block harmful new postal rules from taking effect. We had two. Now we have one. But most importantly, **nothing changes for mail ballots right now.** However, USPS is ready to launch its new rules and last Friday night (very late, because they thought we wouldn’t notice?) they published the details. **It would require election officials to provide voter data to the post office.** It would require all ballot envelopes to be pre-scanned and verified before they could be mailed. It would give them the power to reject ballots for mailing. **That’s objectively a terrible idea,** so what’s next? Fortunately, **the Supreme Court did not rule that Trump’s executive order is constitutional or that the USPS rule is legal.** The Court basically said Colorado and the other states sued too early, before USPS had finalized its rule and before anyone was negatively impacted. Well, now the rule is final. The legal arguments all change, so you can be sure this fight is not over. For now, the second court order still prevents USPS from implementing these changes for November. But **I don’t want to downplay how serious this is** , and how significant an impact it could have on our elections. Election officials could be forced to make major changes to mail voting on an extremely short timeline. I am very concerned. **I'm concerned, but not complacent.** I'm reading the rulings, collaborating with others across Colorado and around the country. I’m planning for what we’ll need to do if the election landscape shifts again. **I’ll keep you updated** the next time somebody in Washington decides ballots should only be delivered during a full moon by certified carrier pigeon, or whatever big idea comes next. **We can’t get complacent about this race, either.** Colorado’s next Secretary of State will be responsible for protecting our elections through the rest of this administration and preparing us for 2028. subject: A major decision from the Supreme Court on mail-in voting
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
This could have major impacts on military members, overseas citizens, the elderly, recently naturalized citizens, and voters with disabilities who rely on mail voting.
#
Hi there,
Tomorrow marks 10 weeks until Election Day, and today the Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) issued a decision that could allow the Trump administration to push through an Executive Order restricting mail-in voting.
This comes after Trump, who claims that vote-by-mail cost him the election in 2020, issued the Executive Order back in March. The order requires that the Postal Service only deliver ballots to individuals on a state-specific list—voters not on this list would be restricted from mail-in voting.
This could have major impacts on voters, including military members, overseas citizens, the elderly, recently naturalized citizens, and voters with disabilities who rely on mail voting.
As always, the Trump administration is looking to make it harder for Americans to vote, because they know Republicans are in danger of losing the House and the Senate this November.
**What you need to know: This isn’t the end of the road for mail-in voting. Today’s ruling changes nothing for voters. The states—not Trump or the USPS—still run our elections.** SCOTUS ruled on a technicality, not the legality of the order. Again, nothing changes for voters right now. There is still a nationwide court order preventing implementation of this Executive Order, and there are potentially more legal challenges, too. We’ll continue to update you as we learn more.
**In the meantime, this SCOTUS ruling won’t change anything we do at Swing Left. It just makes our work to win races in swing districts and states even more important, so that Democrats can win majorities by margins too large for Trump to contest by false mail-in voting claims or otherwise.**
Trump won’t stop, so neither can we. The most impactful thing we can do right now is support candidates and volunteers who talk to voters in competitive races, so we can net enough votes that these efforts by the Supreme Court and the Trump administration won’t have an impact this November.
If Trump’s order ultimately moves forward, campaigns and candidates will need the resources to adapt quickly, as they’ll need to invest in more ads and larger field programs to contact voters about the changes to mail-in voting.
[**If you’d like to arm Democrats with the financial power to weather changes to their races and keep reaching voters, give now to Swing Left’s Balance of Power Fund.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260824-2561&t=1&akid=2561%2E1562180%2EGfA7jF)

This fund supports the Democrats running in the most important House and Senate races that will determine control of Congress next year, in addition to supporting Swing Left as we work to organize in competitive states and districts across the country.
Thank you, as always, for your support.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. clean_body: This could have major impacts on military members, overseas citizens, the elderly, recently naturalized citizens, and voters with disabilities who rely on mail voting. Hi there, Tomorrow marks 10 weeks until Election Day, and today the Supreme Court of the United States (SCOTUS) issued a decision that could allow the Trump administration to push through an Executive Order restricting mail-in voting. This comes after Trump, who claims that vote-by-mail cost him the election in 2020, issued the Executive Order back in March. The order requires that the Postal Service only deliver ballots to individuals on a state-specific list—voters not on this list would be restricted from mail-in voting. This could have major impacts on voters, including military members, overseas citizens, the elderly, recently naturalized citizens, and voters with disabilities who rely on mail voting. As always, the Trump administration is looking to make it harder for Americans to vote, because they know Republicans are in danger of losing the House and the Senate this November. What you need to know: This isn’t the end of the road for mail-in voting. Today’s ruling changes nothing for voters. The states—not Trump or the USPS—still run our elections. SCOTUS ruled on a technicality, not the legality of the order. Again, nothing changes for voters right now. There is still a nationwide court order preventing implementation of this Executive Order, and there are potentially more legal challenges, too. We’ll continue to update you as we learn more. In the meantime, this SCOTUS ruling won’t change anything we do at Swing Left. It just makes our work to win races in swing districts and states even more important, so that Democrats can win majorities by margins too large for Trump to contest by false mail-in voting claims or otherwise. Trump won’t stop, so neither can we. The most impactful thing we can do right now is support candidates and volunteers who talk to voters in competitive races, so we can net enough votes that these efforts by the Supreme Court and the Trump administration won’t have an impact this November. If Trump’s order ultimately moves forward, campaigns and candidates will need the resources to adapt quickly, as they’ll need to invest in more ads and larger field programs to contact voters about the changes to mail-in voting. This fund supports the Democrats running in the most important House and Senate races that will determine control of Congress next year, in addition to supporting Swing Left as we work to organize in competitive states and districts across the country. Thank you, as always, for your support. — The Swing Left Team Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power. body:
Why October money won't help me| | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137851376/642196036/724950626?refcode=260824-oct-money-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMTZiZmZmMi0yM2EwLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlmMWQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AdxVoaNa6WL8rqfkpDro0NJM6cwrkG524ck82YD0Y-U=)
---
I want to explain how campaigns actually work, because it matters far more than most of the fundraising deadlines you hear about. Television time gets bought months in advance. The main House Republican super PAC booked its fall advertising back in the spring. They reserved $153 million worth of ads across the country, the biggest initial reservation in the group's history. Nearly $7 million of that is already reserved against me here in Southwest Washington. And that's just one Republican group. Donald Trump's MAGA Inc. is sitting on more than $400 million. Elon Musk has authorized at least $100 million in spending to help Republicans this fall. These aren't numbers someone made up for a fundraising email. This is money that already exists. And Republicans know exactly which races they need to win. **And I’m at the top of their list. **So when millions of dollars in attacks start running against me this fall, we can't wait until then to figure out how we'll respond. The money to answer them needs to already be sitting in our account. I know this is not the most exciting email I could send you. name: James Carville
subject: Stopped me cold...
body:
It’s
Carville.

UVA's Center for Politics — one of the most respected election forecasters
in the country — updated its race ratings, and now New Hampshire is listed
as the most competitive Democratic-held seat in the country.

They see what we see — one-point polls, an onslaught of outside spending
attacking Chris, and a candidate from a political dynasty with statewide
name ID.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260824_3.9DxGn9&refcode=em20260824-3&t=1001&akid=8500%2E582294%2EGC3ZTA ]🚨 Rush a contribution to Chris Pappas right now. New Hampshire just
became the Senate race that needs your attention most.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260824_3.9DxGn9&amount=5&refcode=em20260824-3&t=1020&akid=8500%2E582294%2EGC3ZTA ]Donate $5 »

Let me tell you what this rating change means in plain English. The
forecasters are telling us that Chris Pappas in New Hampshire – a state
Kamala Harris narrowly won – is now on shakier ground than any other
Democrat running in a currently blue Senate seat.

Why? Because John Sununu — yeah, those Sununus — is a uniquely dangerous
opponent. He's got the famous last name and a Republican machine that has
over $25 million in TV reservations and Koch-backed super PACs already on
the air. He's the kind of candidate that can win in a purple state like
New Hampshire if we don’t treat him like the threat he is.

The forecasters see how close this race is.

The GOP sees what a huge opportunity they have.

I need you to see that this is the most important Senate race in the
country for you to pay attention to right now.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260824_3.9DxGn9&amount=5&refcode=em20260824-3&t=1039&akid=8500%2E582294%2EGC3ZTA ]Donate $5 »

Here's what I keep coming back to: The ratings are shifting in Democrats’
direction in other Senate races across the country, but our chances in New
Hampshire aren’t moving because it’s not getting the same level of
attention.

That’s why I am telling you this: Right now, dollar for dollar, Chris
Pappas is where your investment in a Democratic Senate majority matters
most.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260824_3.9DxGn9&refcode=em20260824-3&t=1040&akid=8500%2E582294%2EGC3ZTA ]Rush a contribution to Chris Pappas today. $10, $25, whatever you can
spare. Because if we keep treating New Hampshire like it's someone else's
problem, we're going to wake up in November one seat short of a majority.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260824_3.9DxGn9&amount=5&refcode=em20260824-3&t=1059&akid=8500%2E582294%2EGC3ZTA ]Donate $5 »

I've been warning about New Hampshire for months. The forecasters just
caught up. Now I need you to step up for Chris right now.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260824_3.9DxGn9&refcode=em20260824-3&t=1060&akid=8500%2E582294%2EGC3ZTA ]Give what you can right now. Let's win this damn thing and flip
control of the Senate.

— James Carville

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260824_3.9DxGn9&refcode=em20260824-3&t=1061&akid=8500%2E582294%2EGC3ZTA ]James Carville

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

| | | | | | Hello Peter,

Tomorrow, I’d love to see you in West Chester!Please join us for **From Conversation to Congress: A Meet & Greet Reception** — an opportunity to come together, talk about the issues affecting our communities, and discuss the kind of leadership we need in Washington.

### FROM CONVERSATION TO CONGRESS
###
**Meet & Greet Reception with Dr. Vanessa Enoch**📅 **Tuesday, August 25, 2026**
⏰ **6:30 PM – 8:00 PM**
📍 **Hummus & Pita**
7334 Tylers Corner Dr.
West Chester, OH 45069
This campaign is about more than winning an election. It is about listening to people across Ohio’s 8th Congressional District and turning those conversations into **real solutions and real impact**.
I want to hear from you.
What issues are affecting your family? What concerns do you have about our community and our country? What should Congress be doing differently?Come meet me, bring your questions and ideas, and learn more about our vision for building a stronger future for the people of Ohio’s 8th District.

### RSVP TODAY
**RSVP here:**
[ https://campaignhq.app/rsvp/hummusandpita](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=141e20202c&e=c6e7dff14c)
And please bring a friend, neighbor, colleague, or family member. The more people we bring into the conversation, the stronger our movement becomes.
**Your Voice. Your District. Your Campaign.**
I hope to see you tomorrow evening!
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Democratic Nominee for U.S. Congress
Ohio’s 8th Congressional District
[https://enochforcongress.com](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=4460636033&e=c6e7dff14c)
**Donate:** [https://enochforcongress.com/donate-now](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=3faa64af2a&e=c6e7dff14c)
**Volunteer:** [https://campaignhq.app](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=fabb2c8921&e=c6e7dff14c)
_Paid for by Committee to Elect Enoch, Catherine Johnson, Treasurer._
* * *

[](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=2ef0223887&e=c6e7dff14c)
# YARD SIGNS ARE GONE!

WE NEED YOUR HELP TO REPLENISH THEM!!!

### GET ON THE WAITING LIST TO GET A YARD SIGN BELOW:

[https://enochforcongress.com/product/free-yard-sign/](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=76ca914060&e=c6e7dff14c)
After you request yours, encourage a neighbor, friend or family member in the district to request one too.
**Let's make support for this campaign visible throughout OH-8.**
* * *

# COME MEET DR. ENOCH
We also have several opportunities coming up to meet Dr. Vanessa Enoch, talk about the issues, and get involved in the campaign.[****](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=da18c409ab&e=c6e7dff14c)
## MEET THE CANDIDATE
### Major Minor Books and Such
**Thursday, August 27**
**7:00 PM – 8:30 PM**
_Doors open at 6:45 PM_**Major Minor Books and Such**
6718 Montgomery Rd.
Cincinnati, OH 45236
Come meet Dr. Enoch and hear about her priorities for Ohio's 8th Congressional District, including protecting Social Security and Medicare, lowering healthcare and prescription drug costs, strengthening veterans' services, creating jobs, expanding affordable housing, investing in American manufacturing, and holding government accountable.
Bring your questions — and bring a friend. [RSVP here](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=8a148533e2&e=c6e7dff14c).
* * *
[](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=b39440c437&e=c6e7dff14c)
## CANVASS GREENHILLS WITH US!
### Canvass for Jonathan Bradner & Dr. Vanessa Enoch
**Sunday, August 30**
**2:00 PM – 5:00 PM****Drummond St. & Damon Rd.**
99 Drummond Street
Greenhills, Ohio
The Cincinnati Working Families Party Wolf Pack is organizing a [canvass covering **Greenhills A, B and C. RSVP on Mobilize here.**](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=1d3b3a4bbf&e=c6e7dff14c)
No canvassing experience is necessary. **Training will be provided.**
Bring a fully charged phone, comfortable walking shoes, and a friend.
* * *
# WE HAVE A LOT OF WORK TO DO — AND NOT A LOT OF TIME.
This campaign is growing.People are volunteering.People are requesting signs.People are attending events.People are knocking doors.And voters are beginning to hear our message.
**Now we need to scale.**
That requires resources.When you contribute to this campaign, you aren't simply making a donation. **You're helping us communicate with voters who may otherwise never hear about this race.**
You're helping us put up the signs.You're helping us run the ads.You're helping us print the literature.You're helping us knock the doors.You're helping us build the field operation.And ultimately, **you're helping give voters in Ohio's 8th Congressional District a real choice.**

### Please make a contribution today.

**DONATE:**
[ https://enochforcongress.com/donate-now/](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=5659e303ff&e=c6e7dff14c)
**REQUEST A YARD SIGN:**
[ https://enochforcongress.com/product/free-yard-sign/](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=c3867f7635&e=c6e7dff14c)
**VOLUNTEER:**
[ https://campaignhq.app](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=3fae20fdd1&e=c6e7dff14c)
[Whether you can give **$10, $25, $50, $100, $250 or more** , your contribution moves us closer to the resources we need to compete.](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=0e8592ad42&e=c6e7dff14c)
**We can do this — but we have to do it together.** Thank you for believing in this campaign and in what we are working to build for Ohio's 8th Congressional District.
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Democratic Nominee for Congress
Ohio's 8th Congressional District
**Enough of Excuses. It's Time for Results.****Real Leadership. Real Solutions. A Stronger Ohio.**

name: Mary Peltola
subject: I’m officially running in the general election for U.S. Senate in Alaska
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| Hello -

My name is Mary Peltola, and after winning last week's primary, I am officially running in the general election for United States Senate in Alaska.

I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together.

But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to join our fight for fish, family, and freedom, please use this button to split a contribution between my campaign for U.S. Senate and the Voter Protection Project: | [CONTRIBUTE »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126285?t=6&akid=28068%2E878179%2Ej-YhMw)
---
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.

They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.

**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**

So I am asking:

[Please split a contribution between the Voter Protection Project and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today as we begin the general election. We are looking for a huge number of day one donors to get our general election campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast to give us the resources we need to WIN in November. ](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/126285?t=7&akid=28068%2E878179%2Ej-YhMw)
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Mary Peltola and VPP will go through immediately:

Thank you,

Mary

| Here's what these numbers mean in plain English.
We are four points down in a state that was supposed to be a MAGA lock.
A fourth-generation farmer from a small town called Waterproof is within striking distance of becoming the first Black senator from Louisiana since Reconstruction!
But here's the OTHER number that really matters: 22% of voters are undecided in this race.
In a race this close - that's the whole ballgame!
That's where you come in.
Every undecided voter we reach with our message -- about fighting corporate corruption, lowering healthcare costs, standing up for working families -- is a vote we can win. But reaching them takes phone banks, digital ads, mailers, and boots on the ground.

## Supreme Court OKs Trump Mail-in Vote Restrictions
The Supreme Court on Monday [cleared the way](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-upSAQxp8GOwyOipyCYhu7s-2WBmE4skExMGr27Tfc-wi3m2S-P_l9f97L24QYjs9vs6Mmn5YDnxKRCPOymxDvROH4ZCyUg6WQjlLQLiBAcqE4jIuxFG5cBtM47REB-wZ1N6lJjgBCNptWHmzXv1blp26VMK5KDMaj8s6rTvqhCbrmCQVjJ0QPsnVgXqg6HCYzrasa2SDQBUq5_ZvCQRv6-C_dmFub9ibqjegsrP_FYGYwP8_T2rVUjvpnMNeTwVyuM-OO3KYrE6d87SeviPybkafsMPOrnIW7rRqarN35hBhDkRMbxKeqvzrph1PdGv4HAAD__zGugO8) for President Trump to move ahead with his executive order restricting mail-in voting before November's midterms. The three liberal justices dissented from the unsigned order. The March order, which Trump casts as a safeguard against fraud and noncitizen voting, directs the government to build lists of eligible voters and bars the U.S. Postal Service from delivering mail ballots to anyone not on them. The agency [published its rule](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAQQL8Gd6zwGBu2oEhDd6dIlyilhWF2PScWLMC28veRc59w3UgjvZn3_rzNb44ipee7e6FpjzwnPGvE1rDML0fxyI3Ss2BthXyjnGpFP4OAiQvNYZydb3TgLF0XzAMRcOjQ9EqraQQQU7ca59Udwr1HJUBOo1-CH0a5yPDQMgQ3dGQuntAw9kIMMN0CuDvqHqVyaln0yKTAQC2X22em1FZ8xL_5wHLz-dVFs7a2VTb8YGAZ2PM8b_tG146B_ZW3-R3PysD-_mBgr0sMrNDXDAzsz1ybi_wDy0Ee-bYvkeqKlV_2nBL_KsDLHpEHrBs15D7vpXFKn3v6isLA9mq6tKUEqQUD2xUTtpNipDopJsXzAv7_uH0z9GHgXwAAAP__3X2SEg) for carrying that out last week. After Trump signed the order in the spring, Democrats in 23 states and D.C. sued, arguing the Constitution gives states and Congress power over elections. A Massachusetts judge [blocked the order](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAMQL8mbEHBBEiHDF3YXteOKDcxF1eBoMSA7t9XaaX-QLcjWbZ8zs-v5ctRpOP9w-1oeU3LgU-JyIx52R3FOzEd74yFM3mmdJSCfgEFo1RGwrA4z3Tjol0T7IoI2Ddou8lM4wCgxmazWgU03aS7QQdnuimsqjdj_xoGvSoEbMjWe8rA0CnVw9gGcN_QdKgnN71eZhBaYSBOuf2V6OAN1_hJN-bWp72JdmM-i-i_C5gFzM_ztFepGnUsYK4oYD5TJCZf0WUmH7HiPxMtYC7XmXFH6dOVWfqILhfJG8rHfeSasuR87aesXeTfMDLlgFnSIV243eFRplXuFBjzXppsw_lQjFTGSWj1rot_fub_TH1b-B0AAP__UnGWIQ) nationwide, and 12 Republican-led states backed the administration's appeal. Now it's a race against the calendar. Some states start mailing ballots within weeks, and the Postal Service itself [said in July](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpiAQBp8GMywcFTEguMTsv_RCC2H05wrFglF3336LjTbfZMKe7u_fa34ZH_yx_TU7alrjfOCTAxJhmnfjwx3JH1vCTMlb8vHIGe0MAiQXikM_G0v-xrkzldMrImBboW4GNcgeQMjqrZteNdB2Ug5ONdbIHkQ3jojr2AI6AZXXhScU9I0QLcjagRlRNdgNZlgW1bNOoPMUU_0_-oPeuIbPeGOqbdyroN9EZ2btHwYTg-l5nvqOhAsaqmPaGEyHKeYmMJjKJwaTUOW0DCZK137yfJ0Jd-Q2Xol4CeeLCSES_5nO8QPtVXp5TA4Tv_KZGUxV0u58fAg-y4F1YiuAbzn65aa3hq8AAAD__5vgjTg) it was running out of time to make the changes. About 30% of all 2024 ballots were cast by mail.
## US Begins 'Economic Outcast' of Iran

Flying over the Atlantic Sunday night, passengers on a red-eye to Rome felt the plane suddenly drop. Then the captain came over the intercom and said one of the engines had "blown out." Inside the cabin, some passengers prayed while others screamed, fearing this flight might be their last. clean_body: I need your help to finish what we started. | We're almost to the finish line, Fellow Patriot, but we cannot slow down yet, because I need your help. We're behind where we should be, even though we've accomplished so much in just over 30 days. Just over four weeks ago, I officially got into this race. Less than two weeks ago, voters in South Carolina cast their votes for the Primary Special Election. Now, I am asking for your help AGAIN to help us win this Runoff Election. I am not a politician - and I think that's a good thing. My opponent has had 20 years to build up his campaign war chest. I have not. What I do have is almost thirty years of working for the people of South Carolina, the values Lindsey and I were both raised on, Every dollar we raise between now and when polls close today matters now more than ever. name: Democrats.org
subject: $7, not more →
body:
---
Derek, Our end-of-month fundraising deadline is approaching fast, and once it’s here we’ll have to report how much we’ve raised in August. It’s no secret that _everyone_ will be looking at our fundraising total. But there’s another number that we’ll be watching that is just as important: The number of people who’ve chipped in this month to help elect Democrats up and down the ballot and across the country this November If everyone receiving this email [**chipped in $7**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-august-2026-gfr?amount=7&refcode=em_20260825_8437_fr&refcode2=8437_22930333_8DMfNK&akid=8437%2E22930333%2E8DMfNK) , we would shatter fundraising records — but the truth is, less than 1% of people reading this will give today. name: Roy Cooper
subject: This decision wasn’t made lightly
body:
I can’t do this alone, Peter.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1155&source=&t=1&akid=2929%2E124072%2ETxvv8E)
| | | |
---
Peter, I’m in a bit of a bind.
A brand-new poll shows that our race is now statistically tied, and the Senate GOP’s top super PACs are currently spending more here in North Carolina than anywhere else in the country. That’s because Senate control hinges on this battleground race.
Since I’m running a grassroots campaign, I can’t fight back without you. So if you’re able to chip in a few bucks to power our fight today, I’d really appreciate it. Here’s the link to donate:
[**_https:/actblue.com/donate_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1155&t=8&akid=2929%2E124072%2ETxvv8E)
Now, my decision to run for Senate wasn’t made lightly.
Serving as Governor was one of the great experiences of my life, but after my second term, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie. From adding hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs to giving school teachers much-needed raises to expanding access to Medicaid, my #1 priority was to improve the lives of everyday people – and we did that.
That’s why it’s so upsetting to see how Washington DC insiders have turned their backs on hardworking people. Insiders like Michael Whatley, my opponent in this race.
My opponent says he’ll lower costs, but he built his career promoting the interests of Big Oil and utility companies at the expense of working families. He says he’ll protect our communities, but as chair of the state GOP, he appointed a convicted child sex offender who served six years in prison to powerful leadership roles within the party because he could raise money. He claims he’ll fight for North Carolinians, but it’s clear that **_his_ priority is choosing himself and his wealthy friends.**
_It’s no wonder why the President anointed him to run after Thom Tillis bowed out of running for this seat._
So while I didn’t plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn’t stand by and watch the GOP rip away health care access, gut resources for public education and chip away at the middle class. They are not making this country “great again.”
I had to get back in the fight, and I’m so glad I did.
Ever since launching this campaign, hundreds of thousands of folks like you have joined our grassroots movement for change, and momentum is on our side.
The hard part will be maintaining it for the next ten weeks or so left in this race.
Republicans are spending nearly $100 million so far to turn voters against me and save their Senate majority – and this surge of dark money is taking a toll on our narrow polling lead.
We can fight back and win in North Carolina, but just as in elections past, I can’t do it alone.
**[_Please, Peter – will you chip in what you can today to help me flip this seat, retake the Senate for Democrats and return power in Washington DC to the hands of working families?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1155&amount=5&t=9&akid=2929%2E124072%2ETxvv8E)**

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

clean_body: I need your help to finish what we started. | We're almost to the finish line, Peter, but we cannot slow down yet, because I need your help. We're behind where we should be, even though we've accomplished so much in just over 30 days. Just over four weeks ago, I officially got into this race. Less than two weeks ago, voters in South Carolina cast their votes for the Primary Special Election. Now, I am asking for your help AGAIN to help us win this Runoff Election. I am not a politician - and I think that's a good thing. My opponent has had 20 years to build up his campaign war chest. I have not. What I do have is almost thirty years of working for the people of South Carolina, the values Lindsey and I were both raised on, Every dollar we raise between now and when polls close today matters now more than ever. It helps us compete with the millions my opponent has put into this race. Our campaign wouldn't be here without the grassroots support of people like you. Right now, I need you with me more than ever.
